Nayak, learned counsel appearing for the State in OPID.
3.

The petitioner is in custody in connection with EOW Bhubaneswar P.S. Case No. 9 of 2023 corresponding to T.R. Case No. 02 of 2023 pending in the Court of learned Designated court under OPID Act, Cuttack for the alleged commission of offence under Sections 420/467/468/120-B of IPC and Section 6 of OPID Act.

sentences.text: 4. The petitioner was earlier granted interim bail for a period of four weeks as per order passed by this Court on 15.05.2024 and extended till 25.10.2024 as per order dated 29.08.2024 considering the fact that he had been granted interim bail in a connected case.

The petitioner was released accordingly and surrendered to custody after expiry of the stipulated period, i.e., on 26.10.2024.
5.

An affidavit has been filed today in Court stating that the petitioner is ready with three demand drafts of Rs.50,000/- each drawn in favour of the three informants, who have already been paid a sum of Rs.15 lakhs in all by the co-accused, who have been released on bail.

sentences.text:
Mr. R.P. Kar, learned Senior Counsel appearing with Ms. A Mishra submits that this amount has been arranged with much difficulty by taking a hand loan from his cousin and because of his incarceration, he is not in a position to pay any further amount.
7.

Mr. Anil Kumar Nayak, learned counsel appearing for the State in OPID matters has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail by submitting that the total amount involved in the case is more than amount Rs.3 crores and therefore, the petitioner's offer cannot be treated as reasonable so as to be shown any leniency.
Mr. Kar submits that the amount due to the informants are actually much less.
At this juncture, Mr. Kar, learned Senior Counsel submits that if the petitioner is released at least on interim bail, he would prove his bonafides by arranging some further amount.
8. Mr. Nayak submits that the Court may pass appropriate order in this regard.

9. Considering the submissions as above and particularly, the prayer of the petitioner to release him on interim bail for some time in order to enable him to arrange further amount to be deposited in the court below, I am inclined to take a lenient view.

It is therefore directed that the petitioner shall be released on interim bail for a period of three months to be reckoned from the date of his actual release on such terms and conditions as the court below may deem fit and proper to impose including the following conditions:-
i. He shall deposit the demand drafts prepared by him in favour of the informants in the court below before his release.
ii. During the period of his interim bail, he shall make endeavour to pay further amount to the informants or deposit the same in the court below.
iii. He shall surrender his passport, if any, before the Court below at the time of release on bail.
10. List the bail application on 19th February, 2024 for hearing.
(Sashikanta Mishra) Judge B.C. Tudu Signed by: BHIGAL CHANDRA TUDU
